title: Which Countries Do Australians Still Need a Visa For?
metaTitle: Which Countries Do Australians Need a Visa For? 2026
metaDescription: Australians still need a visa for India, Vietnam, Russia and Brazil, an ETA for the UK and an ESTA for the US. The 2026 exception list and onward ticket rules.
excerpt: An Australian passport gets you into most of the world with no paperwork, so the useful list is the exception list. content:
An Australian passport opens most of the world with no paperwork at all, but the exception list is longer than people expect. India, Vietnam, Russia and Brazil all want a visa or an e-visa approved before you fly, while the UK, the US and Europe sit in a middle category where you need a pre-authorisation instead of a full visa. China, oddly enough, has gone the other way and is visa-free for short stays.

Which countries do Australians still need a visa for?

Australians still need a proper visa or e-visa for India, Vietnam, Russia and Brazil, four places Australians often assume are easy. The UK asks for an ETA, the US asks for an ESTA, and Europe will ask for an ETIAS once that system starts. China is visa-free for stays of up to 30 days until 31 December 2026.

  • Visa or e-visa needed before you fly: India, Vietnam, Russia and Brazil.
  • Pre-authorisation rather than a visa: the UK (an ETA) and the US (an ESTA), with Europe adding ETIAS once it starts.
  • Nothing needed for a short stay: China for up to 30 days, the Schengen area for 90 days in any 180, and Türkiye for 90 days in any 180.

That is the short version, and the detail per country is where people get caught out. The rest of this guide goes through the big ones, then covers the friction that actually stops Australians at the airport, which is proof of onward travel rather than a visa at all.

Does an Australian passport need a visa for China?

No, not for a short trip. The Chinese Embassy in Canberra confirms that ordinary Australian passport holders can enter China without a visa for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit, with each single stay capped at 30 days. The arrangement was extended again in November 2025 and now runs to 31 December 2026, per the embassy's notice on the extension of the visa-free policy.

Two things narrow it. The waiver covers ordinary passports only, so official and diplomatic passport holders follow different rules, and anything beyond 30 days or outside those listed purposes means a standard visa applied for in advance.

Border officers still expect to see where you are going next. A visa waiver removes the application, not the question at the counter, and a one-way booking into China will draw attention from the airline before it draws any from immigration.

What does India require, and why does the e-visa ask for an onward ticket?

India requires a visa from Australians every time, with no visa on arrival. The usual route is the e-Visa through the Government of India's own portal, which lists Australia as an eligible nationality and offers 30-day, one-year and five-year tourist options alongside business, medical and transit types.

The condition most people miss is written into the official rules. The Indian e-Visa instructions state that "International Travellers should have return ticket or onward journey ticket", and separately require at least six months of passport validity when you apply. Entry is also limited to designated airports and seaports.

So an Indian application is the clearest case for a flight reservation. You need a flight itinerary in the file before you have any reason to commit to dated flights, which is what a dummy ticket for a visa application is for. If you are weighing that against buying the real fare first, we have gone through the maths in should you buy a flight ticket before visa approval.

Do Australians need a visa for Vietnam?

Yes. Vietnam has no visa-free arrangement for Australian passport holders and does not offer them a visa on arrival, so you arrange it before you travel. The national e-visa system at evisa.gov.vn takes applications from Australians directly.

The current e-visa runs for a maximum of 90 days and comes in single-entry and multiple-entry versions, with official fees of USD 25 and USD 50 respectively. Older pages on the immigration portal still describe a 30-day single-entry visa, which is the 2017 pilot and out of date, so work from evisa.gov.vn and nothing else.

Plan the dates properly. The e-visa expiry has to sit at least 30 days inside your passport validity, and the application wants your intended entry date and port, which is harder than it sounds if you have not booked flights.

Can Australians get an e-visa for Russia?

No. Russia's unified electronic visa is open to citizens of 52 listed states and Australia is not one of them, so an Australian application goes through a Russian consulate as a standard visa. Visas are not issued on arrival either.

There is a bigger problem than the paperwork. The Australian Government's Smartraveller advice for Russia sits at "do not travel", Russia does not recognise dual nationality, and some Australians have been placed on an entry ban list. Read the current advisory before you spend anything on an application.

Why do Australians need a visa for Brazil now?

Brazil reinstated a visa requirement for Australian, Canadian and US citizens from 10 April 2025, after years of waiving it. The replacement is an electronic visitor visa, the VIVIS e-visa, covering tourism, business, transit, sport and artistic activity for stays of up to 90 days.

Applications are handled online through Brazil's authorised provider, and the government's own guidance tells you to hold the approved e-visa before you buy airline tickets. You do not need a purchased ticket to apply, which is the same shape of problem as India, where the file wants an itinerary rather than a commitment.

Consular pages also list proof of funds and a planned itinerary among the supporting documents, and the figures differ between posts, so read the current list on the official page for your application rather than a summary of it.

Do Australians need anything for the UK, the US or Europe?

All three now want a pre-authorisation, and all three are easy to forget because none of them is called a visa. The UK charges £20 for an Electronic Travel Authorisation, and the official ETA guidance confirms Australians need one rather than a visa, including for landside transit where you pass through UK border control. Every traveller needs their own, babies included.

The US runs Australians through the Visa Waiver Program, which means an approved ESTA, an e-passport and a stay of up to 90 days. CBP carrier guidance also lists a return or onward ticket as a program requirement, so the onward-travel question is baked into the US rules rather than left to the gate agent.

Europe is the one in motion, and it has two separate changes running at once. The Schengen area still gives Australians 90 days in any 180 without a visa, and the EU's Entry/Exit System became fully operational on 10 April 2026, replacing passport stamping with biometric registration of each entry and exit.

ETIAS is the other half and it is not live. The European Commission's official ETIAS page says the system is "currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point", with a fee set at EUR 20 for whenever it starts and a promise of several months of notice.

The start date has shifted more than once, so treat any specific date you read with suspicion. Nothing is required from you yet, and any website charging you for an ETIAS today is selling you air.

Which countries should you check before you pay for a visa?

Rules move in both directions, and paying for something you no longer need is as common as turning up without one. Türkiye is the clearest example for Australians, since holders of ordinary Australian passports are now exempt from visa requirements for tourism and transit for 90 days in any 180-day period, after years of needing an e-visa.

China went the same way. Treat every list you find online as a starting point, then confirm on Smartraveller or the destination government's own immigration site within a week of travel.

Where is the real friction for Australian travellers?

It is the one-way booking, not the visa. An Australian heading off on a long trip through Southeast Asia or South America typically books a one-way flight and works it out as they go, and that is exactly the passenger an airline will stop at check-in.

The reason is liability. Carriers are fined when they bring a passenger an immigration officer refuses, so the check happens at the departure gate against the destination's entry rules. Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and most of South America all expect evidence that you are leaving, and the person asking is a check-in agent reading a database, not a border officer using judgement.

That is a scheduling problem more than a money problem. You cannot name an exit date six weeks out, but you cannot board without one either, which is what an onward ticket is built for. We have broken down what agents and officers actually accept in what documents prove onward travel to immigration.

How does one flight reservation cover both jobs?

A flight reservation is a real booking that has not been paid for and ticketed. We create it in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport, so it carries a live six-character PNR with your name, flight numbers, dates and the airline's own record, and it reaches you by email in minutes.

That single document answers the visa file and the check-in desk. A consulate wants a credible itinerary to assess your stated travel, and a check-in agent wants a booking in the system that shows you leaving, and both are reading the same reservation.

One detail to understand before you travel. Verification is GDS-primary, which means the reservation is validated in the airline reservation system where it was created, and most airlines display only ticketed bookings on their own websites. A live unticketed reservation often will not appear in a "manage my booking" lookup, and Emirates and Etihad are the usual exceptions.

That catches people out when they test the PNR on an airline site the night before flying and see nothing. Check-in agents and consular staff query the GDS, not the public booking page. For the full picture of how the airport side plays out, read can you use a dummy ticket at airport check-in.

We sell flight reservations and nothing else. Travel insurance can be arranged by email on request, and we do not provide hotel bookings, so plan accommodation separately.

How much does a flight reservation cost in Australian dollars?

Three validity windows, priced in Australian dollars on our Australia page. A 2-day reservation is AUD 19, a 7-day reservation is AUD 28, and a 14-day reservation is AUD 31.

Pick the window from the deadline you are working to. A check-in on a one-way flight needs the reservation live on the day you travel, so 2 days is usually plenty, while a visa application sitting with a consulate for a week or more wants the 7-day or 14-day option so the booking is still valid when an officer opens the file.

Choose your route and dates, pay, and the PNR lands in your inbox. If you are still deciding between a reservation and a fully refundable fare, our comparison of the two covers the cost and the risk of each.

What should you do before you book anything?

Work in this order and the paperwork stops being stressful. Check the destination's current requirement on Smartraveller and the destination government's immigration site, apply for the visa or pre-authorisation you actually need, then put a flight reservation in the application rather than a purchased ticket.

Buy the real fare once the visa is approved and your dates are fixed. For a one-way departure, add a reservation for the day you fly so the check-in desk has something to look at, and head to the Australia pricing page when you are ready.

faqs.question: Do Australians need a visa for China in 2026?
faqs.answer: No. Ordinary Australian passport holders can enter China without a visa for business, tourism, family visits, exchange or transit, with each single stay capped at 30 days. The Chinese Embassy in Canberra extended the arrangement to 31 December 2026. Official and diplomatic passport holders, and anyone staying longer than 30 days, still need a visa.

faqs.question: Does India's e-visa require a return or onward ticket?
faqs.answer: Yes. India's official e-visa instructions state that international travellers should hold a return or onward journey ticket, and your passport needs at least six months of validity when you apply. A flight reservation with a live PNR satisfies the itinerary requirement without locking you into dated flights before approval.

faqs.question: Can Australians apply for a Russian e-visa?
faqs.answer: No. Russia's unified electronic visa is limited to citizens of 52 listed states and Australia is not among them, so Australians apply for a standard visa through a Russian consulate. Visas are not issued on arrival. Smartraveller's advice level for Russia is do not travel, so check it before spending anything.

faqs.question: Is ETIAS required for Australians travelling to Europe?
faqs.answer: Not yet. The European Commission says ETIAS is not in operation and no applications are being collected, with a EUR 20 fee set for whenever it begins and several months of notice promised. Australians currently travel visa-free for 90 days in any 180, with biometric registration under the EU Entry/Exit System.

faqs.question: Will an airline stop an Australian flying on a one-way ticket?
faqs.answer: It can. Airlines are fined for carrying passengers who are refused entry, so check-in staff verify onward travel against the destination's rules. Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and much of South America expect proof you are leaving. A flight reservation showing an exit flight clears the counter without committing you to a fare.

faqs.question: How much does a flight reservation cost from Australia?
faqs.answer: Pricing on our Australia page is AUD 19 for a 2-day reservation, AUD 28 for 7 days and AUD 31 for 14 days. Each one carries a real six-character PNR created in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport and arrives by email within minutes of payment.
